notes.title: Devlog - Important update
notes.content:
Gamers,

The game is still in development phase but the story is almost integrated. There have been changes on it, basically because there was merely one till now. Thanks to this change the game has solidified itself as a investigation game keeping the mechanics introduced in the demo... 

... which has now a small intro and outro in order to stablish it inside the story of the game. 

The page of the game has new additions like images, descriptions in order to help you know what awaits in Stuff to do, in addition to a teaser the captures the atmosphere of the game.

Because of the changes of the game and a development decission the game will be available, for the moment, in two languages.

More soon.

notes.title: Devlog - . . . . -
notes.content:
Greetings,

Although I haven't said anything for a while, I'm still working on the game. There was a big problem and I had to start the project from scratch. This will affect the release date, however it has been good for me to reorganize. 
I have been forced to alternate the development of this game with a totally different one. You have to take advantage of opportunities.
Yesterday David Lynch passed away. One of the references I have for this game is his movie Lost Highway.
The game is still progressing. I had to change aspects and replace mechanics. There are many aspects to take into account, sometimes too many for one person: give information, how to give it, will the player understand it, etc.
One thing is clear and I will not back down on this: everything will be integrated within the game. You will understand this later.


Thanks for still being there.

notes.title: Devlog # . . ___
notes.content:
Hello, gamers,

More people have been playing the demo and adding the game to the wishlist. Thank you. I was planning to remove it for a while, however it will still be available at least for two more weeks. It has been updated.
A kind player recommended me this game Last Half of Darkness, which I must admit, caught my attention right away.
Looks like you are all enjoying the atmosphere of the game. That and the gameplay are aspects that I see myself thinking a lot. Although this project is a "small one", the game design is still an important task (and an adventure).
Which leads me to this: I am sacrificing a coherent arquitecture for the sake of the gameplay. Don´t worry, I am not talking about going upstairs using stairs that lead down. Actually, looks like my games could share the "incoherent arquitecture" tag.
Speaking about other games (mine): next week a Steam Festival will be announced and one of my games (the first one) will be there amongst other known games of the genre. If you enjoy old-school point and click adventures please check them out. 

The game is moving forward. I am a solo developer and there are a lot of things to keep in mind.
See you in two weeks.

Keep playing.

Check your pulse.

notes.title: Devlog # . ____
notes.content:
Hello, gamers.

 Despite not having had any promotion and not having been able to broadcast it, Stuff to do has received a lot more attention than I expected, which I'm quite happy about.
 Actually I thought that the only thing that I would obtain would be a polished version of the demo (yes, it lacked some fine-tuning of the mechanics and a few things here and there). In fact, thanks to the impressions of two people, the demo has had a substantial improvement, more bearable and playable. In today's patch I've added small details to better understand the final puzzle.
 Is pressing Alt+F4 that annoying?
This week will be about scraping off some burrs from the demo and continue with the main game. The mechanics are looking interesting (I'll probably talk about this in next week's post). Obviously the changes for the better in the demo will be reflected in the main game, so I will have to be careful.

Developer tip: if the programming works, don't remove anything.

Thank you very much. Play the demo and discuss it with your friends and close friends. 

Check your pulse.
